titulo: Fix it with robot data: delta action and friends
lead: Sometimes the gap doesn't fit in two parameters. The idea behind ASAP (RSS 2025) is to learn the missing action: a model that, added to the command inside the simulator, makes it repeat what the real robot did. In this lesson you fit a minimal version of that idea with the bench log and measure the simulator's error before and after.
objetivo: fix the simulator with robot data using a delta action model and measure the sim × real tracking error before and after.

aprende.t: The four ASAP stages: pre-training, collection, delta model, fine-tuning
A linear toy of the idea: 8 coefficients by least squares
When to use sysid, when to use delta action

hero_alt: Hands on a keyboard in front of two monitors showing trajectory curves and a simulated robot, with a humanoid robot hanging from the gantry in the background.

secoes.sub: Click each block. The four stages are in the README of LeCAR-Lab/ASAP.

nos.detalhe: The policy learns the task in the simulator, as usual (massive RL).
The policy runs on the real robot and records states and actions. In ASAP, the motion file needs the "action" key. Here, the gantry log from lesson 3 plays that role.
It learns a corrective action δ(s, a) that, added to the command inside the simulator, makes the sim reproduce the real trajectories. In ASAP it is a network trained with RL.
The policy goes back to training in the simulator with the delta model switched on, which now behaves like the robot. Then, back to the robot again.

secoes.legenda: ASAP showed agile skills on the G1 with this cycle. The kit only does stages 2 and 3, in miniature.

secoes.titulo: The kit's toy (and what it is not)
secoes.sub: delta.py, with the log.npz from lesson 3. Click each step.

texto: Per leg joint: δ = a·(target − q) + b·dq, recalculated every 20 ms (the policy step) and added to the target inside the simulator.
mujoco.minimize.least_squares looks for the 8 numbers that make the simulator, replaying the log's command with the correction, reach the positions the robot measured.
Comparing the whole trajectory, rather than one step at a time, keeps the hidden latency from confusing the fit.
A negative a pulls the target toward the current position: the simulator is imitating a softer, slower motor. Together with the kp of 0.6 and the 20 ms latency (delay), that makes sense.
This is not ASAP: there, the delta model is a network with the full state, trained by RL on GPU, and the policy is tuned afterward. Here it is 8 coefficients and no retraining.
It shows the idea working on CPU, in minutes.

secoes.sub: It uses the same log.npz from lesson 3. It takes 1 to 2 minutes on CPU (each evaluation repeats the 4 s of the bench test).

abas.html:
log: ~/fth/log.npz · correção recalculada a cada 20 ms · δ = a·(alvo − q) + b·dq por junta
  left_hip_pitch     a = -0.66  b = -0.013
  left_hip_roll      a = -0.48  b = +0.006
  left_knee          a = -0.66  b = +0.011
  left_ankle_pitch   a = -0.71  b = +0.031
erro de rastreio sim × real: antes 8.16° → depois 3.82° (RMS das posições)
saída: 0

Before, the simulator misses the leg positions by 8.16° (RMS). With the correction, 3.82°. It exits 0 when the error drops.

abas.rot: Common mistake: one step at a time
abas.html: The first version of this script fit δ segment by segment (20 ms), linearizing the simulator in each segment, and the error got worse instead of dropping. The 20 ms latency (delay) makes an isolated segment look like an even softer motor, and the correction overshoots. Fitting against the whole trajectory fixed it: always check the error after the correction, never just the fit.

secoes.sub: Make the simulator imitate the robot.

exercicios.texto: For each case, write which one you would use: (1) the new battery made the robot 2 kg heavier; (2) the knee transmission has backlash that changes with temperature.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: In ASAP, what is the delta action model for?
opcoes: To replace the policy on the real robot.
To make the simulator reproduce the real robot's trajectories.
To measure the network latency (delay) between the onboard computer and the robot.
To raise the motors' kp in the deploy.
perguntas.explica: It corrects the simulator, not the robot. With the simulator corrected, the policy is tuned again and goes back to the robot.

perguntas.p: delta.py fits 8 coefficients. What sets it apart from the real ASAP?
opcoes: Nothing: ASAP also uses a linear model per joint.
ASAP does not need data from the real robot.
ASAP uses the same model, but only in MuJoCo.
There it is a network trained by RL, and the policy is retrained.
perguntas.explica: The kit shows the idea in small scale and on CPU. Saying what it is not is part of the method.

perguntas.p: Fitting segment by segment made the error worse; against the whole trajectory, it got better. Why?
opcoes: The latency (delay) makes each isolated segment look worse than it is.
Short segments have less encoder noise.
The optimizer only accepts 4 s trajectories.
Segment by segment, the model's kp changes by itself at every fitting step.
perguntas.explica: With 20 ms of latency (delay), the response of one segment depends on the command from the previous segment. Looking at the whole lets the fit see that.

itens.texto: Delta action learns the action that is missing for the simulator to imitate the robot.
Eight coefficients take the sim × real error from 8.16° to 3.82°.
Known parameter: sysid. Effect without a clear parameter: delta action.
